precepts.text: Three: the wilderness of Sin. The whole congregation murmured: would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number three is the wilderness of Sin. “And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness”. Do you notice a trend here?

“Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.”

It is going to be the same thing when Christ comes back, but Christ is not playing games with us this time; he did not play games back then either. This time it will be ten times worse, ten times more severe, ten times more strict. When we are saved out of this modern day Egypt, Babylon the Great, America, the United Snakes of America, and Christ brings us into the wilderness, that grace is finished. No more I should have, could have, would have, I made a mistake. That is over with.

precepts.text: Four: hoarding the manna. Moses gave specific instruction, let no man leave of it till the morning; notwithstanding they hearkened not, and it bred worms and stank.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number four is the hoarding of the manna. “And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.” Moses gave specific instructions: do not leave any of the manna until the morning.

“Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.” Moses just told you. And they said, the hell with you; we want to replace you anyway. That is the mindset of our people.

This is what the Lord means in Numbers 14:22 when he says they “have not hearkened to my voice.” He fed them bread from heaven, gave one plain instruction, and they would not keep it.

precepts.text: Five: gathering on the Sabbath. The Lord gave two days of bread on the sixth day, and they went out on the seventh anyway. How long refuse ye to keep my commandments? No gratitude at all.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number five is the Sabbath manna. “And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none. And the Lord said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws? See, for that the Lord hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.”

They were supposed to gather extra on the sixth day; the Most High gave them enough manna to lay up for two days. And they said, no, Lord, we are going out on the seventh day to get this manna. Forgetting everything the Most High did for us in bringing us up out of Egypt. No gratitude. We are a people of no gratitude at all.

precepts.text: Bake that which ye will bake today: lay up your food before Friday sundown, because there is no cooking on the Sabbath.
precepts.point: On the seventh day God ended his work which he had made, and he rested on the seventh day. The seventh day is not Sunday. Seven represents completion, perfection; hold that, because the whole class hangs on it.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Keeping the seventh day holy means more than not going to the job. Exodus 16:23 shows how the food is handled: “To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.”

So before Friday sundown, before complete darkness, you are to lay up your food for the next day, because there is no cooking on the Sabbath. Whatever needs baking or boiling is done the day before, and what is left over is kept for the holy day.

This is one of the laws that apply to the Sabbath, and it follows from Genesis 2:2-3: God “rested on the seventh day from all his work,” and he “blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.” His people rest the same way, preparing ahead so that the seventh day stays free of labour.

precepts.text: The seventh day is a sabbath of rest, an holy convocation in all your dwellings; Exodus 16:29 does not undo the gathering.
precepts.point: For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith.

note.label: Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved

precepts.why:
“abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.” That is about not going out to gather food on the sabbath; some of the people had gone out on the seventh day to gather and found none. Some foolish Israelites read verse 29 out of context and say you never have to leave your house or join a congregation on the sabbath. That is not what it says.

The sabbath is a holy convocation. “Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein: it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.” A holy convocation is a large gathering, and it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings, so we are to come together on it. Exodus 16:29 does not undo the gathering; it stops the going out to gather food.

precepts.text: Greet the church that is in their house, and Epaenetus the firstfruits of Achaia; congregations begin with the diligent few.
precepts.point: For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith.

note.label: Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved

precepts.why:
For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation, the sabbath as a holy convocation is still the order. You may have to travel, and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area.

That is how it began. Paul writes, “Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus”, and “Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.” The first assemblies met in houses, and Epenetus was the firstfruits of a whole region. Congregations begin with the diligent few, and that is how camps start: a church in a house, and a first one in the area.

precepts.text: Seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added; the Lord sees the sacrifice it takes to get to the congregation.
precepts.point: For the brothers and sisters far from a congregation: you may have to travel and you may have to be the firstfruits in your area. The first assemblies met in houses, and that is how camps start; a man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth, and the Lord honors that faith.

note.label: Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved

precepts.why:
Getting to the congregation on the sabbath takes sacrifice, especially for those far from one. “But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.” Seek the kingdom first; the rest is added.

A man will drive hours to a club, so drive for the truth. The Lord sees the sacrifice it takes to get to the congregation and honors that faith. The sabbath is the holy convocation, and he who seeks first the kingdom to keep it is the one all these things are added to.

precepts.text: Bake that which ye will bake to day, and that which remaineth is laid up until the morning; the sabbath food is cooked the day before.
precepts.point: The Lord gives no man license to sin, but Christ is Lord of the sabbath and brought grace for necessities out of our control, a blown tire or an empty tank on the way to keep the sabbath, or medicine when the body is in danger; it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.”

The sabbath food is cooked the day before. What is baked and seethed is prepared and laid up, so the sabbath meal is leftovers or simple food; eating is allowed, cooking is not. That is how “in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord” is kept in the kitchen.

precepts.text: Bake that which ye will bake today, and lay up what remaineth to be kept until the morning; kindling fire on the sabbath goes to cooking, so the cooking was done on the preparation day.
precepts.point: Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day: kindling fire goes to cooking. Bake that which ye will bake today, and seethe that ye will seethe, and lay up what remains to be kept unto the morning; you could not cook on the sabbath, so the day before is the prep day, and what you prepare that day is what you eat.

note.label: Exodus 35: The Sabbath and the Willing Hearted Offering

precepts.why:
“Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” Kindling fire goes to cooking. “To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.”

You could not cook on the sabbath, so the day before is the prep day. What you bake and seethe that day is laid up, and what you prepare that day is what you eat on the seventh day, the holy day, the sabbath of rest to the Lord.

precepts.text: The Sabbath rest concerning the preparing of food, another precept on what the law of the Sabbath was.
precepts.point: They insist Christ broke the Sabbath even though Peter and Paul testified that Christ did no sin, which shows the same spirit that was on the Pharisees is on the Christian pastors. The work the Sabbath forbids is occupational labor, not healing or picking corn to eat, and their real motive was envy, because the disciples gathered and unified the people and their control and money were being touched.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Another precept on what the law of the Sabbath was: “To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.”

The Sabbath rest concerns the preparing of food, done the day before. Line these precepts up and the work forbidden is plain, and none of it is what Christ or the disciples did.

Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: The whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness: would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: The whole congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron: would to God we had died in Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots and did eat bread to the full. They wanted to go back to Egypt for dependency on Egypt, not realizing how much greater a thing God had in store for his people.

Christ was saying in Matthew 4:4 that your spirit needs daily nourishment to survive the wilderness. And make no mistake, this is a wilderness. The Bible says we are pilgrims and strangers here; this is not our rest. This is a proving ground where we have grace, much like our forefathers had forty years of grace, to get it right.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day. There was a portion for each day, and it was different for everyone: based on appetite, family size, your needs, because everybody needs a different level of nourishment. Some of us need more than others when it comes to the nourishment of the word of God.

That I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no. Were they not keeping the Sabbath? What he is really talking about is whether they would stay on him daily, seeking him as the source and the supply.

The perfect scenario is you read your four chapters a day, you watch a class, you have it all set up. But life is not always thrown at us that way. You can listen to something; you can read a couple of verses at a bare minimum, and not just random verses. The things that are most heavy unto thee, seek them out in the scripture and meditate on them. Sometimes too many verses is not good; maybe what you lack is to focus on one or two verses that get you right on what you are dealing with.

The Bible talks extensively about bitterness and grudging, yet we still fall into it. That is how you know that somebody who says they are leaving because they are offended by somebody, and claims they will still keep God's laws, is not being honest. They left because they held a grudge and grew bitter against somebody, and then left. You have to be careful when feelings start coming up about people that are personal, and not about the sin they are doing.

I will be candid: I am not in it every day, and I feel it when I am not. It does not manifest like hunger or thirst, but it is your mind that starts to stray; it is your spirit that starts to look at things differently. The ones that are most seductive and subtle are the things that deal with emotions, what you feel about others, or the weariness you get in the mission.

The bread we were given to eat, the spiritual food from heaven, was talking about Christ.

Not that it has no value; it is not enough. You need to eat every day, and you need to be in the word every day.
